## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `intent-ambiguity-hedging`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-25T06:21:11.864Z.

(24) Intent-ambiguity hedging via risk-adjusted portfolio selection. Entry (19) conditions the weight vector on a known task intent; entry (4) then packs greedily by marginal value per token. Both assume the intent is identified. In practice the opening call of a session is exactly where intent is least certain, and committing the whole budget to the single most probable intent is the highest-variance play available. Treat selection as portfolio construction over a posterior across intents: each candidate has an expected value under each intent hypothesis, and the objective becomes expected value minus a variance penalty scaled by posterior entropy. Concretely, maintain the intent posterior from the invoking command, recent history, and claim state; compute per-candidate value vectors under each hypothesis; select the subset maximising expected marginal value per token less lambda times the cross-hypothesis variance of that value, with lambda annealing to zero as the posterior sharpens. High-entropy openings therefore buy coverage across plausible intents; sharp posteriors reduce exactly to (19)+(4) with no separate code path. The envelope discloses the posterior and lambda so the hedging is explainable and testable, and pm-atfm gains a natural judgment class: ambiguous-opening scenarios where a hedged pack must beat a committed one.



## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
